ALTERNATIVES TO THE ACTION
The basic alternatives considered are: a. Take no action, b. Extend the scope of the standard to NPA's above 6,000 pounds GVWR, c. Make the standard effective for years beyond MY 1979, and d. Set a higher or lower standard.
With regard to the alternative of taking no action, section 502(b) of the Motor Vehicle Information and Cost Savings Act directs the Secretary of Transportation to prescribe automotive fuel economy standards for automobiles which are "not passenger automobiles" in model years which begin more than 30 months after the date of enactment of Title V. (December 22, 1975). Model year 1979 is the first model year that begins after the 30-month period. As a minimum, Title V requires that an automotive fuel economy standard for nonpassenger automobiles of not more than 6,000 pounds GVWR must be issued. Section 502(b) also requires that such a standard be issued not later than 18 months before the beginning of the model year.
If projected yearly growth rates for NPA's and passenger automobiles continue, by 1985 NPA's of 6,000 pounds and less GVWR will consume 20 percent of the total fuel consumed
